name: tovel
author: time-agent
description: tovel v4. Clue "L/S/x/k/n": L = days in the month (28-31), S = the column the 1st falls in (0 = Monday), x = a capital letter, k = 1..5, n = a date. The answer is that month's page: week rows of seven cells, the first row starting in column S, the dates 1..L in reading order, and EVERY date carrying a capital letter (token = the date immediately followed by its letter, e.g. "17B"). A weekday header line is allowed and ignored (any line containing no digit is skipped); whitespace and blank lines are free. RULE (unchanged since v3): score 1 iff the page is exactly right AND the dates d such that d and d+2 BOTH carry x, the day in between (d+1) does NOT carry x, and d falls on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday number exactly k, AND the earliest of them is n - i.e. "x, something else, x - inside the same school week (Mon+Wed, Tue+Thu, Wed+Fri) - exactly k times, and the first time is the nth". WHY v4 (evidence: run lad-tovel-v3-2, two Opus players, plus lad-tovel-v3-1, two Sonnet): v3 is too_hard - four finals 0 %, 0 %, 1.8 %, 0.05 %, kid judge 3.8/5. The rule was not the problem; the missing FOOTHOLD was. v3 closed the v2 stripe so completely that EVERY cheap probe scored 0 (solid stripe 0.00 %, random lettering ~1 %, the minimal pair probe 0.00 %), so both Opus players concluded the grader is exact string match - tovel2b: "Round 3, 461 answers, 8 layout variants: 0 correct -> the letters are graded, exactly"; tovel2a: the letters are "instance-specific data that only a demo can reveal" - and spent the game farming demos (2a cached 7 demos x 26 letter renames, 1.8 % final; 2b cached 7 demos, 0.05 %). 2b's kid-proxy actually SAW the rule's shape in a demo - "20K 21O 22K 23O 24K 25O 26K 27O, far too regular for i.i.d. sampling, so there is structure" - and never tested it, because it believed letters were compared byte for byte. Three of the four Opus players read v3's varying header as a trap; only the v2 theorist ever read it as the leniency hint it was meant to be. THE FIX is three changes in generate() only - the rule, the scorer, the calendar picture and every decoy guarantee are untouched. (1) FOOTHOLD: k now ranges 1..5 with k = 1 on 22 % of clues. On a k=1 clue the smallest natural probe - "x on day n and on day n+2, x nowhere else, anything on the other days" - scores 1. Measured on 600 fresh clues: 22.00 %, i.e. EXACTLY the k=1 share (132/132 of the k=1 clues, 0/468 of the rest), and the same 22.00 % when the other days carry random letters. That one probe hands back the four facts v3 hid: the grader is a predicate over content, the clue letter is what is graded, n is where it starts, and k counts something. k >= 2 still needs the Mon/Tue/Wed clause and the blocked-middle clause, so the foothold is a first rung, not the answer. The k mix is 0.22/0.16/0.16/0.23/0.23 for k=1..5: skewed slightly to the large k because the every-other-day template is near-perfect at k=2 (there it coincides with the rule and cannot be closed) and nearly hopeless at k=5. (2) UNIFORM HEADER: every demo now prints " Mo  Tu  We  Th  Fr  Sa  Su". v3 rotated three styles as a deliberate free hint that the grader is not comparing text; the measurement is in - 1 of 6 Opus players read it that way, 3 of 6 read it as a trap - so the hint goes and the foothold does that job honestly. (3) n SITS LATER for k >= 2: n is the max of six uniform draws over the days that still leave room for k non-adjacent counted starts (v3: max of three, for every k). An every-other-day run needs about 14k/3 days of room while the rule needs only about 7k/2 (counted starts may be packed Mon+Wed inside one week), so pushing n late starves the template without touching the rule. For k = 1 n is the max of two draws only: the template IS the rule at k=1 so lateness buys nothing there, and a mid-month n leaves room before n for the decoys that make a k=1 demo readable. WITNESS TABLE, 600 fresh clues, v3 -> v4 (scratchpad time4/attack.py; the template rows fit the best run length per cell on the same clues, i.e. an optimistic ceiling): minimal probe "x on n and n+2, nothing else x" 0.00 % -> 22.00 % (= the k=1 share exactly; with random other letters, 0.00 % -> 22.00 %); SOLID STRIPE from n, best length per k, every length 3..16 0.00 % -> 0.00 %; ALTERNATING x . x . x from n with a per-k length table 46.00 % -> 50.83 %, with a per-(k, weekday of n) table 56.17 % -> 57.67 % (per k in v4: k=1 100 %, k=2 91.7 %, k=3 61.5 %, k=4 37.2 %, k=5 11.5 % - the large-k clues can still only be answered by someone who knows which pairs count); WEEKLY PAIR (the "same day every week" template, pairs at n, n+7, n+14 ...; it satisfies the weekday clause automatically without knowing it, but it is far too long to fit) 31.67 % in v4 (k=1 100 %, k=2 50.0 %, k=3 8.3 %, k=4 1.5 %, k=5 0.0 %); the TIGHTEST Mon/Tue/Wed packing per (k, weekday of n) - which is the rule itself expressed as a 15-cell offset table - 100 %, because generate() picks n only among days that still leave room for k non-adjacent counted starts, i.e. a player who has the rule needs no per-clue search; tuned random lettering at densities 0.20/0.35/0.50/0.65/0.80 0.0/0.3/0.7/0.2/0.2 % -> 0.7/1.0/1.0/0.7/0.7 %; best constant answer 0.50 % -> 1.00 %; demo replay with the letters renamed, same (L,S,k) 2.2 % -> 5.8 %, same (L,S,k,n) 64.2 % -> 70.7 % (the attack that earned tovel2a its 1.8 %: there are 924 distinct (L,S,k,n) classes and 337 effective ones, so six demos cover ~2 % of items); the true rule 100 % -> 100 %. Wrong-relation constructors on a correct page honouring the clue's first day (600 clues, v4): x next door 0.00 %, x three apart 0.00 %, x a week apart 0.00 %, x two apart anywhere 22.00 %, x two apart Mon-Wed = THE v2 RULE 26.50 %, x . x anywhere with the gap kept 30.17 %, the true rule 100.00 % - every one of those now floors at the 22 % of k=1 clues where they all coincide with the rule, and none of them reaches 31 %; ignoring the clue's first day they all fall to 0.00 %. Shape attacks on a page with the correct count are as in v3 (the scorer is byte-identical): header or no header, tabs, blank lines 100 %; one row, one token per line, zero-padded dates, an extra or a dropped day, lower case, "17 B" instead of "17B" 0 %; a page laid out from column 0 scores exactly the S=0 clues. INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH (private): (1) one demo shows a calendar page and "L/S" is its shape - the first row holds 7-S dates; kid-easy, and nothing scores until it is right. (2) day n always carries x, and so does day n+2, with something else in between. (3) THE FOOTHOLD: put x on n and n+2 and nowhere else - it scores on the k=1 clues, which proves the grader reads the letters as a pattern and that k counts these little pairs. (4) k >= 2: where may the other pairs go? Every demo shows, positively, that a pair whose middle day is also x does not count (a blocked x x x run starting Mon/Tue/Wed appears in 100.0 % of demos, one of them BEFORE day n in 94.3 %), and that a pair starting Thursday (it reaches the weekend) or Saturday/Sunday (it steps over the week break) does not count (97.6 % / 99.3 %; some non-counting pair sits before day n in 98.3 %). (5) solve() guarantees that in EVERY demo each of eleven rival counts differs from k (x next door, two apart anywhere, two apart Mon-Fri, a week apart, the number of x's, the same relation for any letter, three apart, two apart with the gap free, that inside Mon-Fri, cells rather than pairs, and the v2 rule itself). Hypothesis-elimination surrogate over 840 hand-built "count a relation between marked days" expressions (distance 1-7 x 10 weekday windows x 3 gap conditions x this-letter/any-letter x pairs/cells): survivors after 1 demo 2-17, after 2 demos 1, in all six trials - unchanged from v3, so the fairness floor holds. VALIDATION: quickcheck --seeds 200 OK, no warnings; score 431 chars (cap 512), solve 4879 (cap 5000), generate 721; clue 11 chars, solution <= 175. generate 0.07 ms, score 0.05 ms, solve 164 ms worst under quickcheck. solve() scores 1 on 3000/3000 fresh seeds across all five k - 669/669, 457/457, 481/481, 746/746, 647/647 at k=1..5 - (95.5 ms average, 197 ms worst) and re-parses its own output before returning it. The scorer never raises and never returns a non-binary value on 20000 random junk strings, scores 0 on empty/spaces/newlines/"0"/"1"/"x"/"1"*100/a 4000-char junk string/the clue itself, and agrees with an independent re-implementation of the stated rule on 9000 mutated well-formed answers with 0 disagreements. Human-designed for the "everyday time and place" direction: the object is a family calendar, the measurement has no name, and recognising the calendar is necessary but nowhere near sufficient. PREDICTED TIERS: blind ~1 %, demo cache with renames ~2 %, the natural first probe 22 %, the tuned every-other-day run 51-58 %, the rule 100 %.
generate:
def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    L = r.choice([28, 29, 30, 31, 30, 31])
    S = r.randrange(7)
    x = r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    k = 1 if r.random() < 0.22 else r.choice([2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5])
    E = [d for d in range(1, L - 1) if (d - 1 + S) % 7 < 3]
    F = []
    for j, d0 in enumerate(E):          # first days with room for k non-adjacent starts
        t = 0
        p = -9
        for d in E[j:]:
            if d - p > 1:
                t += 1
                p = d
        if t >= k:
            F.append(d0)
    i = max(r.randrange(len(F)) for _ in range(2 if k == 1 else 6))
    return "%d/%d/%s/%d/%d" % (L, S, x, k, F[i])   # n sits late: starves the x.x.x template
solve:
def sel(g, S, x):
    # THE RULE: x, something else, x - starting on a Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday
    return [i for i in range(len(g) - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x != g[i + 1] and (i + S) % 7 < 3]


def cnts(g, S, x):
    # counted, rivals that must NOT equal k, wrong-day starts, blocked starts
    L = len(g)
    P = [i for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x]
    C = sel(g, S, x)
    D = [i for i in P if g[i + 1] != x and (i + S) % 7 > 2]
    B = [i for i in P if g[i + 1] == x and (i + S) % 7 < 3]
    H = (sum(1 for i in range(L - 1) if g[i] == g[i + 1] == x),
         len(P), sum(1 for i in P if (i + S) % 7 < 5),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 7) if g[i] == g[i + 7] == x), g.count(x),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] != g[i + 1] and (i + S) % 7 < 3),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 3) if g[i] == g[i + 3] == x),
         sum(1 for i in P if g[i + 1] != x),
         sum(1 for i in P if g[i + 1] != x and (i + S) % 7 < 5),
         len({j for i in C for j in (i, i + 2)}))
    return C, H, D, B


def render(g, S):
    h = "Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su".split()
    cs = [""] * S + ["%d%s" % (i + 1, g[i]) for i in range(len(g))]
    while len(cs) % 7:
        cs.append("")
    o = [" ".join(w.rjust(3) for w in h).rstrip()]
    for j in range(0, len(cs), 7):
        o.append(" ".join(c.rjust(3) for c in cs[j:j + 7]).rstrip())
    return "\n".join(o)


def chk(s, L, S, x, k, f):
    R = [l.split() for l in s.split("\n") if any(h.isdigit() for h in l)]
    T = [t for r in R for t in r]
    if (len(T) != L or len(R[0]) != 7 - S or not 0 < len(R[-1]) < 8
            or any(len(r) != 7 for r in R[1:-1])
            or any(t[:-1] != str(i + 1) or t[-1] <= "9" for i, t in enumerate(T))):
        return 0
    C = sel([t[-1] for t in T], S, x)
    return len(C) == k and C[0] == f


def solve(clue):
    a = clue.split("/"); L = int(a[0]); S = int(a[1]); x = a[2]; k = int(a[3]); f = int(a[4]) - 1
    r = random.Random(clue)
    po = [c for c in string.ascii_uppercase if c != x]
    sl = [i for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 < 3 and i > f + 1]
    room = []   # how much room each slot leaves
    for i in sl:
        t = 0; p = i
        for j in sl:
            if j > p + 1:
                t += 1; p = j
        room.append(t)
    for att in range(1600):
        w = 4 if att < 700 else 3 if att < 1000 else 2 if att < 1300 else 1 if att < 1500 else 0
        ot = r.sample(po, r.randint(3, 4))
        g = [r.choice(ot) for _ in range(L)]
        ch = [f]
        while len(ch) < k:      # never two counted starts side by side
            av = [i for i, t in zip(sl, room) if i > ch[-1] + 1 and t >= k - len(ch) - 1]
            if not av:
                break
            ch.append(av[0] if r.random() < 0.5 else r.choice(av[:3]))
        if len(ch) < k:
            continue
        for i in ch:
            g[i] = x; g[i + 2] = x
        mv = [[(i, i + 1, i + 2) for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 < 3]]   # x x x
        r.shuffle(mv[0])
        mv[0].sort(key=lambda p: not (w > 3 and p[0] < f))
        for want in ((3, 4), (5, 6)):       # weekend-reaching / week-break decoys
            c2 = [(i, i + 2) for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 in want]
            r.shuffle(c2)
            c2.sort(key=lambda p: (not (w > 3 and p[0] < f),
                                   min(abs(p[0] - c) for c in ch) > 3))
            mv.append(c2)
        mv += [[(i, i + 1) for i in range(L - 1)], [(i, i + 7) for i in range(L - 7)]]
        r.shuffle(mv[3]); r.shuffle(mv[4])
        for c2 in mv:
            for p in c2:
                sv = [g[i] for i in p]
                for i in p:
                    g[i] = x
                C = sel(g, S, x)
                if len(C) == k and C[0] == f:
                    break
                for i, v in zip(p, sv):
                    g[i] = v
        fr = [i for i in sl if x not in (g[i], g[i + 1], g[i + 2])]
        r.shuffle(fr)
        for i in fr[:2]:          # another letter, two apart
            c = r.choice(ot)
            g[i] = c; g[i + 2] = c
            if g[i + 1] == c:
                g[i + 1] = r.choice([q for q in ot if q != c])
        C, H, D, B = cnts(g, S, x)
        if len(C) != k or C[0] != f or any(h == k for h in H) or len(set(g)) < 4:
            continue
        p1 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 == 3]
        p2 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 in (5, 6)]
        if w and (not B or not p1 or not p2):
            continue
        if w > 2 and (min(abs(i - c) for i in p1 for c in C) > 3
                      or min(abs(i - c) for i in p2 for c in C) > 3):
            continue
        if w > 3 and f > 0 and not [i for i in B + D if i < f]:
            continue
        if w > 1 and g.count(x) > (0.30 + 0.035 * k) * L:
            continue
        s = render(g, S)
        if chk(s, L, S, x, k, f):
            return s
    return ""
